PullRequest.Title: agentHost: make Allow Once the default approval for every tool confirmation
PullRequest.Body:
fix #342606

Shell, URL, read and write confirmations already listed Allow Once first, but the shared fallback used by every other permission kind (MCP, skill, custom tool, hook, memory, workflow and extension requests) still listed the tool-wide session grant first. Clients make the first approve option the primary button, so a single click granted the tool for the rest of the session.

The fallback now lists Allow Once first, so the default is the same for every kind. Option ids and what each option does are unchanged, the session grant stays in the dropdown, and agent-supplied options (for example plan approval) keep their own order. Managed and sandbox-bypass confirmations stay one-time only, and the documented sandbox path-grant default is not changed.

The smoke approval helper now also accepts the Allow Once primary label, since it previously only clicked "Allow" or "Allow in this Session".

## How to test

In an Agent Host Copilot session with default approvals, trigger a confirmation for a tool that is not a shell command, fetch, read or edit, for example an MCP tool. The primary button reads **Allow Once**, and **Allow in this Session** is in its dropdown. Choosing Allow Once prompts again on the next call of that tool; choosing Allow in this Session does not.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/**/*.test.js"`: 18988 passing, 80 pending, 0 failing. The two updated order assertions failed before the fix.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts`: 2141 passing, 2 pending, 0 failing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed. `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed. `pnpm run compile` in `test/automation`: passed.
- Not run: smoke, integration and end-to-end suites, and no live window was driven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive fallback confirmations for MCP, skill, custom tool, hook, memory, workflow, extension, or unspecified permission kinds; subsequent calls of the same tool.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing host deny/auto-approval evaluation precedes creation and publication of the ready action. Tool execution waits for a user decision; the client dispatches the selected option and the provider's pending permission is resolved. The diff changes the primary decision from a session grant to one-time consent, not the work required to process an individual decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the ChatToolCallReady envelope to connected clients through the existing action transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ready action per permission signal, distributed through the existing subscribers. The fallback still contains exactly three options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same ready action and same three option objects, with the two approve options in the opposite order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The prompt must arrive before the user can approve the tool.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch ChatToolCallConfirmed to the host, which resolves the provider permission request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one confirmation outcome per chat/turn/tool-call/action-type key, enforced by _resolvedToolCalls. Host routing removes the pending route and Copilot resolves its pending permission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same deduplicated confirmation dispatch and provider response. Only the selected option differs when the user chooses the primary action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The tool waits for this decision. No new subprocess or network tool invocation is added by the reorder.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of requested tool calls and concurrently pending confirmations, not total available tools. Button construction remains bounded to three fallback options and two visible grouped buttons.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each request awaits its own decision. Existing pending-confirmation reevaluation iterates sequentially with cancellation; client outcome dispatch remains deduplicated. No new parallel scheduling or global limiter change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing allow rules still auto-approve matching requests. Choosing the session option still adds a deduplicated tool rule; choosing Allow Once intentionally adds no reusable grant and requires consent again on subsequent calls. No positive/negative cache, invalidation, or coalescing code changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the three-option constant, createToolReadyAction fallback, grouped button builder, selected-id dispatch, grant side effect, and provider pending-permission resolution.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of repeated user approvals depends on workflow and selection. No runtime timings were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Repeated consent is the deliberate permission-policy change; the diff does not independently add expensive computation, larger serialization, new boundary fan-out, or lost resource cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scoped shell/URL/read/write approvals, managed approvals, sandbox bypass/path-grant approvals, and agent-supplied options.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing permission checks run before a prompt. Read/write path-grant construction may await filesystem resolution and ancestor discovery before publication. Managed and bypass requests use separate one-time arrays; sandbox path grants and agent-supplied options retain their existing selection and ordering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve literal/canonical paths using realpath/lstat and probe ancestor .git entries to construct scoped grants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per relevant read/write permission request; ancestor probes stop at the first repository root or filesystem root. Nonexistent suffix resolution scales with missing ancestor depth. Fallback MCP/custom kinds do not enter these filesystem branches merely because the options were reordered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical read/write branches, canonicalization, ancestor probing, and scoped option construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaits precede publication of read/write scoped prompts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize host configuration and persist it with mkdir, temporary write, and rename when an explicit persistent host grant is selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only when an explicit host grant changes stored rules; permission rules are deduplicated. Root-config writes remain sequenced through _rootConfigWrite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same explicit host-grant path and serialized persistence. Reordering the tool-wide session/once fallback neither adds nor moves these writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host persistence is queued asynchronously; the one-time fallback choice does not trigger it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing scoped or agent-supplied confirmation options and return the selected decision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing ready/confirmation envelopes per relevant request, with unchanged option cardinality and duplicate-outcome suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Scoped arrays, managed/bypass arrays, and copies of state.options already bypassed the reordered fallback and remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Interactive tool execution waits for the same confirmation flow.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Read/write requests, filesystem path depth, explicit grant-rule count, and provided option count. The changed tests cover a fixed ten-kind table and order assertions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing path resolution awaits and ancestor probes remain unchanged; root persistence is globally sequenced for the service. No new work is scheduled by the constant reorder.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scoped/session/host grants retain their existing deduplication and matching. Path resolution has no new cache; neither its cold nor warm behavior changes. Agent-supplied options still take precedence where they did before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the scoped-kind guard, createToolReadyAction ternary branches, path-grant construction, and configuration persistence implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem speed and path depth vary, but the diff does not change their cost or placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. These paths retain their pre-diff defaults and expensive-boundary counts; nearby filesystem work is pre-existing and not materially amplified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Smoke automation accepts pending confirmations while waiting for chat responses or Dev Container log links.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When confirmation acceptance is enabled, each response/link polling iteration awaits the shared helper before checking progress. The helper reads button elements, verifies the primary label, locates a visible matching button, and clicks at most one.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use Playwright page.evaluate to obtain renderer button elements, then locator count/isVisible/click calls to approve a visible confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing getElements call per polling iteration. For a recognized label, one count and up to the number of matched buttons in visibility checks, followed by at most one click with the existing 2000 ms timeout. The diff additionally recognizes Allow Once; it does not issue queries for all tools or introduce a loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Allow and Allow in this Session used the identical query/visibility/click path. Allow Once returned immediately after the existing element query and could not be accepted by the helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited on opt-in response polls, which already sleep 250 ms in Chat and 100 ms in the log-link loop. Recognizing Allow Once lets the existing confirmation gate progress instead of leaving the tool waiting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The automated click follows the same user-confirmation dispatch to the host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One deduplicated confirmation outcome per clicked tool request, not per polling iteration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical dispatch for recognized primary labels; an Allow Once label prevented the click from reaching this existing path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Allows the pending tool and awaited response/link to proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Opt-in polling iterations and currently matching confirmation buttons. The new regular expression remains fixed-size; selector scope, recursive element retrieval, iteration bounds, and timeouts are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All helper operations are sequentially awaited, and the helper returns after its first visible-button click. Polling is sequential rather than launching overlapping clicks.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retained collection. Once clicked, the existing confirmation lifecycle settles the request; subsequent tool calls may intentionally require their own one-time approvals.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all helper callers, the unchanged selector and loops, and the driver's concrete page.evaluate implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual polling duration and number of visible/hidden widgets depend on the smoke workflow; no automation was executed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression or independently established performance-regression fix. The label expansion restores functional acceptance using the existing bounded path; timeout avoidance alone is not treated as a separate performance mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all six changed files and every diff page against base 95fe7e433943b5cd8a152c6bdd22027147174e1c. Traced approval rendering, permission grants, provider response cleanup, action transport, filesystem grant preparation/persistence, and automation polling. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issues and no qualifying performance-regression fix. Static read-only review; no runtime profiling.
